'''Sibylle Günter''' (born 20 April 1964) is a German [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] researching [[tokamak|tokamak plasmas]]. Since February 2011, she has headed the [[Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ipp.mpg.de/1084794/guenter|title=Prof. Dr. Sibylle Günter|publisher=Max-Planck-Institut für Plasmaphysik|access-date=8 November 2015 |language=}}</ref><ref name=academia>{{cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-dr-sibylle-guenter/1133752|title=Prof. Dr. Sibylle Günter |publisher=AcademiaNet|access-date=8 November 2015 |language=}}</ref> In October 2015, she was elected a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in recognition of her contribution to research.<ref name=mae/>

==Biography==
Born in [[Rostock]], Günter matriculated from high school in 1982. She went on to study physics at the [[University of Rostock]] where she graduated in 1987 and earned a doctorate in 1990 with a dissertation on radiation from [[Dense plasma focus|dense plasmas]]. Her thesis advisor was Gerd Röpke. After working as a research associate at the university's Department of Theoretical Physics, she completed her [[habilitation]] in 1996. Her work in Rostock was complemented by periods in the United States at the [[University of Maryland]] and at the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]].<ref name=academia/><ref name=mae>{{cite web|url=http://www.ipp.mpg.de/3962320/10_15|title=IPP Director elected as member of Academia Europaea|date=13 October 2015|publisher=Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics|access-date=8 November 2015 |language=}}</ref>

In 1996, she joined the Tokamak Physics division of the [[Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics]] (IPP) in [[Garching bei München|Garching]] near [[Munich]]. In 2000, she was appointed director of the institute and head of Tokamak Physics coordinating research on the principles of a [[Fusion power|fusion plant]] designed to produce energy resulting from the fusion of light ions. In 2011, she became IPP's scientific director.<ref name=academia/><ref name=mae/>

In October 2015, in view of her outstanding contribution to research, the [[Academia Europaea]]'s board elected Günter a member of the Academy.<ref name=mae/>
